newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes down led by major issue losses.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes down led by major issue losses.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange lost ground for the fourth consecutive session on Tuesday, as blue chips stagnate while foreign investors wait on the sidelines in fear of a U.S. interest rate hike.
Eight of the bourse's 10 largest issues fell, pushing the PX50 index down 2.7 points, or 0.49 percent, to 550.5, while the Reuters RPIX index closed down 10.4 points at 1,141.8.

Dealers said blue chips such as SPT Telecom, CEZ and Komercni Banka -- which account for some 45 percent -- are extremely sensitive to the mood of foreign investors, who normally account for around half the trading in the two shares.
"The story remains the same, there is no new money coming in. Everybody is waiting for what will happen in the U.S.," Jan Sykora of Wood and Company told Reuters.
Overall, 192 issues rose on the day, while 185 fell and 173 held steady. A total of 1.05 million shares changed hands on turnover of 910.7 million crowns.
Markets across the region have been eagerly awaiting a meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Markets Committee on Tuesday due to widespread speculation that U.S. interest rates may be raised.
